newsitem.title: INDIA: Militants fire at Kashmir ration depot, injure 15.
newsitem.headline: Militants fire at Kashmir ration depot, injure 15.

text.p: Fifteen people were injured on Thursday when militants opened fire on people who tried to stop them looting bags of sugar from a ration depot in the troubled Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir, police said.

Four members of the pro-government Jammu Kashmir Ikhwan militia opened fire indiscriminately at the depot in Kulgam, 60 km (40 miles) south of Srinagar, they said. Four of the injured were in serious condition.

"They started looting sugar bags from the depot and when we tried to stop them the militants opened fire on us," Gulam Mohammad Reshi, one of the injured, told Reuters from his bed in a Srinagar hospital.
More than a dozen militant groups are fighting Indian rule in Jammu and Kashmir, while at least three pro-government militia groups are helping Indian paramilitary troops.
Elsewhere in the Kashmir valley, five people were killed in militancy-related incidents, police said.
Police and hospital authorities estimate that over 20,000 people have died in violence since the Islamic separatist revolt broke out in 1990.
